{{Ship module infobox}}

The '''Business Class Passenger Cabin''' is a D-rated optional internal module for carrying passengers whose missions require Economy or Business Class accommodation. It offers more comfort than an [[Economy Class Passenger Cabin]] but fewer seats in the same compartment, making it the standard middle tier between bulk capacity and premium accommodation.

Business cabins can be fitted to any ship with an ordinary optional internal compartment of the required size. They cannot be installed in Military Compartments.

Cabin mass is fixed. Boarding passengers does not increase it, and an empty cabin weighs the same as an occupied one. Higher classes provide more seats but can make a noticeable difference to jump range, especially when several cabins are fitted.

Business cabins draw no power and cannot be engineered.

== Accommodation quality ==

A passenger can be placed in a cabin that meets or exceeds the class stated by the mission:

* Economy passengers can use Economy, Business, First or Luxury accommodation.
* Business passengers can use Business, First or Luxury accommodation.
* First Class and Luxury passengers cannot use a Business cabin.

Using Business accommodation for Economy passengers is valid but carries fewer passengers than an Economy cabin of the same size. The higher-quality cabin does not change the mission's contract, destination or passenger count.

== Passenger occupancy ==

Passenger cabins use seats rather than cargo capacity. Passengers cannot be moved into a Cargo Rack, and cabin seats cannot carry commodities.

For bulk passenger contracts, groups can share available seats and may be divided among multiple cabins of the same qualifying class. VIP parties behave differently: one VIP mission reserves an entire cabin for its party, even when unused seats remain. That cabin stays assigned until the contract is completed, failed or abandoned.

A Business cabin can therefore be efficient for several ordinary groups requiring Business accommodation, while a small VIP party may leave much of a larger cabin unusable for other contracts.

== Acquisition and compatibility ==

Standard Business Class Passenger Cabins are sold for credits through Outfitting. Availability depends on local stock, but no permit, Engineer or Technology Broker unlock is intrinsic to the module.

Classes 3–6 fit ordinary optional internal compartments of the same or greater size. A larger cabin can be placed in an oversized compartment, but it keeps its original seat count; the unused compartment size provides no additional capacity.

== Mk II Business Passenger Cabins ==

The Live game also has Mk II Business Passenger Cabins with 50% more capacity than their standard counterparts. Frontier introduced them with the Lynx Highliner in update 4.3.3.0, and they can only be fitted to that ship.

Mk II cabins are a separate ship-specific line. Their extra seats do not change Business accommodation rules, and they are not available in Legacy.

== Choosing a cabin ==

A Business cabin is appropriate when a contract explicitly requires Business accommodation or when a commander wants to keep capacity available for both Economy and Business missions. Economy cabins remain more space-efficient for Economy-only bulk transport, while [[First Class Passenger Cabin|First Class]] and [[Luxury Passenger Cabin|Luxury cabins]] are required when a contract specifies those higher tiers.

Before accepting a mission, compare its passenger count, minimum accommodation and VIP status with the actual free cabin configuration. Total empty seats alone do not guarantee that the party can be assigned.
